name: reviewer-dev-via-test decide(rejected_retry) with NO subtopics → coordinator ask_user (fail-safe)
description:
ADR-044 §addendum Slice 5 — corruption-to-no-op fence (go-reviewer C1). CBG's rejected_retry verdict REQUIRES a subtopics=[<task-id>] naming which task to re-implement (rule 07c stamps it as the retry target). But the decide tool makes subtopics optional and stamps coordinator.decision.subtopics only when non-empty, and the rule engine has no unresolved-token guard on triple OBJECTS — so a rejected_retry emitted without subtopics would let 07c stamp a literal garbage target. 07c is fenced to fire ONLY on subtopics.length>0; this rule catches the complementary case (rejected_retry + subtopics.length=0) and escalates to the user instead of silently mis-targeting or wedging the chain (07c wouldn't fire, so nothing would wake the coordinator).

Mirrors rule 07b (CBG rejected → ask_user) — same final-coordinator wake-up, because a rejected_retry CBG can't pin to a task is, operationally, a plain rejection the user must resolve. Mirrors rule 01's lineage length_eq 0 fence: convert a malformed decision into a safe escalation, never corruption.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
The dev-via-test chain you dispatched has reached its terminal — NOT cleanly. CBG (reviewer-dev-via-test) at loop $entity.instance rejected the work and judged it dev-fixable (rejected_retry), but did NOT name which task to fix (no subtopics). Without a target task, the chain cannot auto-re-dispatch — so this falls to you to surface to the user.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result(loop_id=$entity.instance) to read CBG's verdict. CBG's reason explains what's wrong.

Iteration 2 — call decide(action="ask_user", reason="<surface CBG's finding to the user; explain the reviewer wants a fix but didn't pin it to a specific task; ask them to amend the plan or abandon>"). One question, plain prose, addressed to the user. The user replies and a fresh coordinator loop fires on their answer.

metadata.review_origin: go-reviewer C1 (2026-06-05): rejected_retry without subtopics would stamp a garbage target via 07c. Fence 07c on subtopics.length>0 + this rule on subtopics.length=0 = mutually-exclusive split, mirrors rule 01/03's subtopics differentiator.
metadata.mutually_exclusive_with: 07c-cbg-retry-stamp.json (fires on rejected_retry + subtopics.length>0). This rule fires on rejected_retry + subtopics.length=0. No double-fire; every rejected_retry routes exactly one way.
metadata.anchor_disposition: anchor_threaded (ADR-053 Phase 4b-1a, TestAgentRunPack_CoordinatorSpawnCoverage) — threads run-loop-entity-id from $entity.triple.lineage.run-loop-entity-id onto the woken coordinator so its involuntary failure routes to agent-run/06. Fires on reviewer-dev-via-test (chain-end CBG), which always carries lineage.run-loop-entity-id (threaded by rule 06), so no split is needed.
